Name: Ferngill News Network
Author: CozyPsychologist
Description:
[center][size=5][b][u]Ferngill News Network[/u][/b][/size][/center]

[size=4]A daily wartime news channel for Stardew Valley.

The war between the Ferngill Republic and the Gotoro Empire is one of the biggest pieces of Stardew Valley’s background lore, but outside of Kent’s story and a handful of references, the player rarely hears about what is actually happening beyond the valley.[/size]
[size=4]
Ferngill News Network expands that part of the world by adding a new television channel hosted by Mara Bell, a Ferngill news anchor covering the war, politics, business, culture, sports, and everyday life across the Republic.[/size]
[size=4]
Every day brings a new broadcast.[/size]

[size=5][u]What does FNN add?[/u][/size]

[size=4]FNN contains a fully chronological storyline covering the first three years of the game and a large continuing-news pool for Year 4 and beyond.[/size]
[size=4]
Each broadcast covers the day’s main war story, a secondary development, and finishes with a segment called Around Ferngill covering civilian life elsewhere in the Republic.[/size]
[size=4]
The goal is to make Stardew Valley feel like one small community inside a much larger country.[/size]

[size=5][u]A War That Develops Over Time[/u][/size]
[size=4]
Year 1 follows the growing Kestrel Crisis, a major Gotoro offensive, Ferngill’s counteroffensive, the fighting around the Kestrel Islands, and eventual negotiations over prisoners of war.[/size]
[size=4]
Year 2 begins with returning POWs and moves into maritime conflict along the Sable Coast, shipping disruptions, diplomatic efforts, shortages, and a temporary Winter Star ceasefire.[/size]
[size=4]
Year 3 focuses increasingly on war fatigue, government transparency, labor unrest, diplomacy, and negotiations. The two governments eventually establish separation zones and an extended ceasefire.
The war does not receive a neat permanent ending. Ferngill and Gotoro remain rivals, disputed territory remains disputed, and the storyline stays compatible with Stardew Valley’s intentionally vague canon.[/size]
[size=4]
From Year 4 onward, FNN switches to a large pool of continuing ceasefire-era broadcasts. These reports can appear in different orders without permanently restarting or ending the war.[/size]

[size=5][u]Around Ferngill[/u][/size]

[size=4]Every broadcast ends with Around Ferngill, a shorter story about something happening away from the battlefield. These reports deliberately do not focus exclusively on Pelican Town.
You’ll hear stories about:[/size]
[list]
[*][size=4]Zuzu City — transit, nightlife, housing, business, crime, arts, restaurants, Joja, and the Zuzu Tunnelers gridball team. [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Zuzu University — agriculture, veterinary medicine, engineering, journalism, archaeology, meteorology, student life, and occasionally questionable slime research. [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Fernholm — the National Assembly, elections, infrastructure, courts, public policy, government audits, housing, and national institutions. [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Havenport — shipyards, docks, maritime industry, freight, ferries, and waterfront redevelopment. [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Larkspur — railroads, manufacturing, industrial labor, warehouses, and transportation. [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Alderfield — an agricultural market town known for grain, dairy, farm cooperatives, agricultural fairs, and university extension work. [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Greyhaven — a northern fishing and shipbuilding town centered around its harbor, lighthouse, fish market, coastal weather, and maritime traditions. [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Copperwell — an old mining community shaped by geology, mine safety, labor history, stonework, and reclamation of former mining land. [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Willowmere — a river town known for old estates, crafts, theater, preservation, confectionery, and a slightly unusual amount of local folklore. [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Joja Corporation — logistics, wartime contracts, labor disputes, retail expansion, shipping, pricing, lobbying, and the transition back toward civilian commerce. [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Everyday Ferngill life — elections, court decisions, transportation accidents, strikes, business openings, crime, public works, education, weather damage, sports, art, odd local stories, and other normal news. [/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]Some Around Ferngill stories also develop across multiple broadcasts. A Zuzu University agricultural project can be announced in spring, tested during summer, evaluated in fall, and eventually adopted years later. Greyhaven’s harbor renovation unfolds over several seasons. Joja labor disputes escalate and resolve. Fernholm elections have consequences. The Zuzu Tunnelers can actually have a season rather than appearing in disconnected sports headlines.[/size]

[size=4][i][b]**Lots of this stuff is not canon. I took some creative liberties to make the world feel more lived in.**[/b][/i][/size]

[u][size=5]Stardew Valley News[/size][/u]

[size=4]Pelican Town still makes the national news when something notable happens.[/size]
[size=4]
FNN includes coverage of the Egg Festival, Flower Dance, Luau, Trout Derby, Dance of the Moonlight Jellies, Stardew Valley Fair, Spirit’s Eve, Festival of Ice, SquidFest, Night Market, Feast of the Winter Star, and the Desert Festival.[/size]
[size=4]
Other familiar events can also make the broadcast, including the reopening of the mountain mines, the earthquake that opens the railroad route, local harvests, fishing, mining, Joja activity, and other recognizable pieces of vanilla lore.[/size]
[size=4]
FNN can also recognize which major development route the player has completed. If the Community Center has been restored, later reports may discuss its return to civic life. If the Joja Community Development route was completed instead, FNN may report on Joja’s increased role in Pelican Town’s infrastructure and economy.[/size]
[heading][u][size=5]Joja Corporation[/size][/u][/heading]
[size=4]Joja isn’t treated as a secret organization controlling the war, and it isn’t reduced to a cartoon villain. Instead, FNN treats Joja like the enormous national corporation Stardew Valley implies it is.[/size]
[size=4]
During the war, Joja receives government contracts, expands logistics operations, moves military and civilian supplies, and benefits from increased demand. Workers organize over hours, safety, and wages. Independent businesses criticize Joja’s influence. Government regulators question pricing and corporate contracts. Later broadcasts follow Joja as it converts wartime infrastructure back toward civilian commerce.[/size]
[heading][size=5][u]A Larger Ferngill Republic[/u][/size][/heading]
[size=4]Ferngill’s Gold — Weekly Editorial

FNN includes Ferngill’s Gold, a long-form weekly travel and human-interest feature hosted by veteran correspondent Hollis Hower inspired by California’s Gold with Huell Howser which ran from 1991-2012. RIP Huell. [/size]
[size=4]
Inspired by old-fashioned local travel programs, Hollis spends each issue visiting the towns, neighborhoods, workplaces, institutions, and unusual corners of the Ferngill Republic that are often only mentioned briefly during the daily news. Each feature focuses on the people who live there, local history, regional traditions, industries, food, folklore, and the small details that give each community its own identity.

After first tuning in to FNN, the player will receive a Special Programming Notice introducing the series. From there, a new issue of Ferngill’s Gold arrives every Sunday.

Features
48 unique issues spanning three full Stardew years
16 issues per year, with four issues each season
Hosted by recurring FNN correspondent Hollis Hower who visits locations including:[/size]
[size=4]
Zuzu City
Zuzu University
Fernholm
Greyhaven
Alderfield
Copperwell
Willowmere
Havenport
Larkspur
Pelican Town
Calico Desert
and other corners of the Republic[/size]
[size=4]
Each issue includes a small souvenir or local item connected to that week’s destination
Stories occasionally revisit the same place from a completely different angle, allowing communities to develop naturally over time.[/size]
[size=4]
Includes subtle connections to Stardew Valley lore, regional history, the war, Joja, transportation, universities, labor, local traditions, and life beyond the valley[/size]

[size=4][b][u]Frequently Asked Questions[/u][/b]

Q: When do the broadcasts air?
A: There's a new one every day.

Q: What happens if I don't watch an episode?
A: The valley does not offer streaming services. You are at the mercy of the airwaves. If you miss it you miss it. 
 
Q: Can I install the mod mid-save?
A: Yes. The broadcasts will align with wherever you're at in your save.  

Q: Will the broadcasts eventually repeat?
A: There's an arc for the war that eventually becomes randomized cease-fire era news stories after year 4. 

Q: Was this mod made with AI?
A: No, each story was written by me. No AI was used for coding.  [/size]

[u][size=5]Installation[/size][/u]

Then unzip Ferngill News Network into your Mods folder.
Launch the game through SMAPI.
The Ferngill News Network channel will appear as a selectable television program.[/size]
